title: Naseeruddin Shah Plays JRD Tata in the Story of How Titan Was Built From Nothing. It Streams Free on June 3.
excerpt: Made in India: A Titan Story traces the unlikely journey from a failed printing press to India's most iconic watch brand. Jim Sarbh plays Xerxes Desai, the man who made it happen.
body:
If you grew up in an Indian household anywhere in the world, there's a good chance your first real watch was a Titan. Maybe a Sonata, the entry-level line your parents bought you for your 10th birthday. Maybe a Titan Edge that an uncle gifted after your board exams. The brand is so deeply embedded in Indian middle-class life that it's easy to forget it had to be invented from scratch.

*Made in India: A Titan Story*, streaming on Amazon MX Player from June 3, tells the origin story of how that happened — and it has the cast to match the ambition.

## Naseeruddin Shah as JRD Tata

Naseeruddin Shah plays J.R.D. Tata, the visionary industrialist who chaired the Tata Group for over five decades and received the Bharat Ratna in 1992. Jim Sarbh plays Xerxes Desai, the man Tata tasked with reviving the struggling Tata Press — who instead pivoted the entire operation into an unknown category: wristwatches.

The series is set in pre-liberalization India, a period when the country was at the cusp of massive economic and social change. Bureaucratic hurdles, market skepticism, and the sheer audacity of competing with established Swiss and Japanese watchmakers form the dramatic backbone.

"Portraying J.R.D. Tata is both a privilege and a responsibility," Shah said in a statement. "He was a man who combined vision with humanity. Made in India is not just about a company — it is about a legacy that continues to inspire generations."

## India's First Startup Story

The series positions itself as "India's first startup story" — which, in the age of Bangalore unicorns and Y Combinator applications, hits differently. Titan wasn't built with venture capital or pitch decks. It was built within a conglomerate by people who had to fight internal politics, government regulations, and a market that didn't believe Indian consumers would buy an Indian watch.

The story follows Desai's journey from that initial failure of Tata Press through the creation of Sonata, the affordable line that cracked the mass market, all the way to the Titan Edge — the world's slimmest watch at the time — which announced India's arrival as a global player in consumer goods.

## Why the Diaspora Should Watch

For NRIs, Titan isn't just a brand — it's a marker of a particular era. The series, directed by Robbie Grewal and written by Karan Vyas, is produced by Almighty Motion Picture in collaboration with T-Series Films. The supporting cast includes Vaibhav Tatwawadi, Namita Dubey, Kaveri Seth, Lakshvir Saran, and Paresh Ganatra.

The show draws comparisons to *Scam 1992* and *Rocket Boys* — period dramas that used Indian business and science history as raw material for genuinely compelling television. If it hits that mark, *Made in India* could be the kind of show that NRI parents and their kids actually watch together, which is about as rare as a genuine horological innovation.

Streaming free on Amazon MX Player from June 3, across the MX Player app, Amazon shopping app, Prime Video, Fire TV, and Airtel Xstream.
author: Diaspora Desk
